text.p: British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc, boosted by the prospect of better-than-expected provable oil and gas reserves, said on Thursday it was moving ahead with plans for the possible development of its Morpeth field in the deep water Gulf of Mexico region.
It expects a formal decision to be taken on field development in the next few weeks.

In an announcement explaining the latest interpretation of an October test well drilling, the company said that, in addition to total proven and probable reserves of 77 mmboe, upside reserves potential was estimated at around 92 mmboe.

"A production test on the main P sand reservoir in the field confirmed a greater flow potential than previously anticipated, leading to a prediction of plateau production at 35,000 bopd, rather than the 25,000 bopd originally envisaged."
In order to maintain what it called "an aggressive project schedule leading to production start up in the summer of 1998", BBPS has already ordered some long lead time items.

Also, the deepwater drilling rig Ocean Endeavor (which British-Borneo has contracted on a term basis) is scheduled to drill and complete two additional production wells and one water injection well, starting in July.
BBPS' wholly-owned subsidiary British-Borneo Petroleum Inc is field operator and holds a 100 percent working interest in it. It now anticipates development costs of about $210 million.
The announcment came as the British company's share price was again surging upwards.

After a strong run since the year-end, amid a combination of takeover bid speculation and some bullish analysts' forecasts, BBPS' share price added nearly 100p in early trade, jumping to an intraday high of 1035 pence.
By 0855, following the release of the Morpeth report, the rise had been tempered and the shares were up 39-1/2 pence at 977-1/2 pence in turnover of less than 200,000 shares.
